clue.text: Rejected and dropped, holding back information

indicators.note: holding means the first word grips the second piece inside it

parts.note: dropped, as a wind or price falls, means abated

indicators.note: back says the word for information is read in reverse

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone's proposal was rejected and dropped because they kept facts to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding back' does two things: 'back' reverses the slang for information to NEG, and 'holding' puts it inside the word for dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To abnegate is to renounce or deny, so something abnegated has been rejected or given up.

clue.text: Dog, black one, grabbing pasta

indicators.note: grabbing means the outer letters seize the pasta word between them

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
one is I, the Roman numeral
orzo is a small rice-shaped pasta

explanation.surface: A black dog snatches someone's plate of pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: A borzoi is a breed of Russian wolfhound, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: See some tigers at zoo, not like the real thing

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Tigers in a zoo are not like those found in the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link inviting you to look at the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means an inferior imitation or substitute, so it is not like the genuine article.

clue.text: Safety device essential in pipes?

parts.note: a car's inflating cushion, read again as the inflated sack every set of bagpipes depends on

explanation.surface: A safety mechanism is vital for plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a valve in plumbing; the question mark warns that the pipes are bagpipes, whose bag is filled with air.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a car's crash cushion and also, cryptically, the wind-filled sack of the bagpipes.

clue.text: Power to harm and be upset, I heard

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for be is turned upside down

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live

indicators.note: I heard signals that the letter is replaced by a word sounding the same

parts.note: the letter I is said like the word for the organ of sight

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have the power to cause harm and to be distressed, from hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LIVE into EVIL; 'I heard' gives EYE, which sounds like I.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a superstitious power to cause harm with a glance.

clue.text: Property mainly belonging to me is kept inside bar

indicators.note: is kept inside means the possessive word sits within the shortened property word
mainly means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: an estate is landed property
something belonging to me is mine

explanation.surface: Property that is mostly mine is held within a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the last letter of the property word, leaving ESTAT; 'is kept inside' then wraps it round the possessive. An estaminet is a French bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French café selling drinks, a kind of bar.

clue.text: Petty rule it could be unpolitic to break

indicators.note: to break means the letters of the word are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Breaking a minor regulation might be impolitic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it could be' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctilio is a fine point of etiquette or conduct, a minor rule to be observed.

clue.text: Top up rum he mixed with Pilsner

indicators.note: rum here means odd or strange, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A drinker tops up a rum mixed with Pilsner lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' reads as the spirit, but it is the adjective meaning odd, signalling the anagram; 'mixed with' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish is to refill, which is to top up.

clue.text: Clever as student, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: a tutee is a student being taught by a tutor

explanation.surface: Someone is as clever as a student, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TUTEE to TUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means shrewd and sharp-witted, synonyms for clever.

clue.text: Material son added to rum and water

indicators.note: added to means the abbreviation is placed into the drink

parts.note: grog is a drink of rum diluted with water, as once served in the Royal Navy
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A sailor's son has been mixed into a drink of rum and water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum and water' is a single definition of GROG; only 'water' gives RAIN. S goes into GROG to make GROSG.
explanation.definitionFit: Grosgrain is a heavy ribbed silk fabric, a material used for ribbons.

clue.text: Scrub cape unusually clean

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape

indicators.note: unusually means the letters are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Someone scrubs a cape until it is unusually clean.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is to call it off, which is to cancel it.

clue.text: ATM George misused as source of money

indicators.note: misused means the letters are put to wrong use, rearranged

explanation.surface: George misuses a cash machine to get money.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortgagee is the lender in a mortgage, the party who supplies the money.

clue.text: Man of great stature eclipsing one as artist

indicators.note: eclipsing means the larger word covers and hides the numeral inside it

parts.note: a titan is a giant, a man of great stature
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A towering figure overshadows a single rival as a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Tiny swimmers, with so little weight, turning up at openings

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means both short words are read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
oz, the ounce, is a small unit of weight
pores are tiny openings in skin or leaves

explanation.surface: Tiny swimmers are so light that they rise to the surface through gaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses SO plus OZ together, SOOZ giving ZOOS; 'with' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoospores are spores that swim by means of flagella, so they are microscopic swimmers.

clue.text: As material, get serge or get terry in part

indicators.note: in part means only a section of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone choosing fabric is told to buy serge or terry towelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' and the first 'get' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgette is a thin crêpe dress fabric, so it is a material.

clue.text: A piteous drunk, having died, examined thus?

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A pitiful drunk who has died is examined in this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-mortem examination is an autopsy, so a body examined that way was autopsied.

clue.text: Secure contract

definitions.meaning: to secure something is to obtain it
to contract an illness is to catch it

explanation.definitionFit: Both obtaining something and catching a disease are senses of the same short verb.

clue.text: What gets grey started?

parts.note: the letter standing at the front of both the words gets and grey, spelt out as a word

explanation.surface: Something makes people's hair start going grey.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about ageing; the answer is the name of the letter G, which starts both 'gets' and 'grey'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spelt-out name of the letter G is what begins words such as grey.

clue.text: Non-alcoholic drink is what driver needs, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a golfer teeing off with a driver needs a tee to rest the ball on

explanation.surface: A motorist must stick to soft drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The driver is a golf club, not a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a common hot drink containing no alcohol.

clue.text: Repeat too much love poetry around university

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: around means the poetry word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Love poetry about university life is overdone.
explanation.definitionFit: To overuse a word or phrase is to repeat it too often.

clue.text: They cover pupils, including learner I had in English? OK

indicators.note: including means the outer letters take in the middle piece

parts.note: saying yes means OK
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A schoolchild asks whether their essay is OK in English.
explanation.walkthrough: Pupils are in the eyes, not the classroom; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelids are the folds of skin that close over the eye, covering its pupils.

clue.text: Character of Timon and others reduced

indicators.note: reduced means the phrase is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: et al is the Latin abbreviation for and others

explanation.surface: A character in Timon of Athens and other plays is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Timon of Athens is Greek, so his character is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character Timon, an Athenian, would write.

clue.text: About a thousand units involved in main disturbance

indicators.note: involved means the letters are entangled into a new arrangement

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: About a thousand units are caught up in a major disruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the sea, not principal; 'About' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave, a disturbance of the main, an old word for ocean.

clue.text: Tailor putting skill in to select cut

indicators.note: putting skill in means the skill word is placed inside the other
cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to sort is to select
art is skill

explanation.surface: A tailor uses craft to pick the right cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims the select word to SOR before 'in' takes the skill word inside; 'putting' and 'to' are links. Sartor is a jocular Latin borrowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartor is Latin for tailor, used humorously in English for one.

clue.text: Authors announced titles

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: titles are rights or entitlements, as title to property

explanation.surface: Writers have made their book titles public.
explanation.definitionFit: To author a book is to write it, so authors as a verb means writes.

clue.text: Like nurses at work, keep going!

definitions.meaning: hospital nurses on duty are working on a ward

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it places nurses at work; as one, it is a call to press ahead.

clue.text: With this kind of coat, unaffected by flak

definitions.text: With this kind of coat, unaffected by flak

parts.words: With this kind of coat, unaffected by flak
parts.note: a non-stick pan coating, used figuratively of politicians whom criticism never sticks to

explanation.surface: A coat of armour makes someone immune to anti-aircraft fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Flak is criticism, and a politician who survives scandals is said to be coated with this non-stick material.
explanation.definitionFit: Teflon is a non-stick coating, and figuratively describes someone to whom criticism never sticks.

clue.text: Odd US candidate who kept spirits up?

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd
in the US one who stands for office is said to run, so a candidate is a runner

explanation.surface: A strange American politician kept people cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping spirits up sounds like morale; it means supplying liquor during US Prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumrunner smuggled liquor, so he kept the supply of spirits going.

clue.text: Port not all passed orthodoxly to the left

indicators.note: to the left means the letters are read leftwards, backwards
not all means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Not every port passed the orthodox approach to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port in Ukraine.

clue.text: Tale's beginning, in fact, in touching way

indicators.note: beginning means only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: actually means in fact

explanation.surface: A story starts, in fact, in a moving way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' means by touch, not moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactually means by means of touch, so in a touching way.

clue.text: Course from France in French plane, say

parts.note: en is French for in
the plane is a kind of tree, common in London

explanation.surface: A French dish is served on a plane flying in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The plane is the tree, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrée is a course of a meal, and the word comes from French.

clue.text: Impression about second team's left-winger, maybe

indicators.note: about means the impression word goes round the others

parts.note: a dint is a dent, an impression left by a blow
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A dent appears around the second team's left-wing footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: A left-winger in politics may be a rebel, not a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident is one who opposes the establishment, as a left-wing rebel might.
